sentences.text: Chaudhary Traders, having its registered office at Batfara Road, Ambha Morena, a lease of sand mining at District Hamirpur was got for a period of five years on 30.01.2018.
It has been further alleged that for the investment in the lease project about Rs.2/- Crore was taken by the applicant from opposite party no.2 Rakesh Kumar and one Brijesh Chandra.

4. The parties signed a notarized agreement mentioning the terms and conditions therein while the applicant requested for investment for the amount of Rs.2/- Crore from the opposite party no.2 Rakesh Kumar and one Brijesh Chandra.
When the applicant did not fulfill the terms and conditions of the aforesaid notarized agreement and did not return the money to the opposite party, the present case was lodged.
5. On 16.05.2022, the following order was passed:-

"Heard Shri I.B. Singh, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Shri Ishan Baghel and Anuj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.G.A. for the State as well as Shri Prabhu Sharan, learned counsel for respondent no. 2 who has filed vakalatnama which is taken on record.
Learned Senior Advocate after arguing the matter at length has submitted that it is primarily a civil dispute between the petitioner and the complainant and both the parties have lodged F.I.R.'s against each other.
It is further submitted that in all likelihood if the matter is referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court, there is a hope that it can be settled amicably through mediation.
Learned counsel for respondent no. 2 has conceded the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner.
In view of the above, the petitioner as well as the complainant is directed to appear before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court on 30.05.2022.
Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court shall submit its report before this Court within three months thereafter.
The petitioner is directed to deposit a sum of Rs. 25,000/- before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court.

Till the next date of listing, further proceedings instituted from case crime No.
312/2020, under Sections 420/406/504/506, P.S. Alambagh, District Lucknow, shall remain stayed."

6. In compliance of the aforesaid order, the parties appeared before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench, Lucknow and on 15.12.2022 and Giriraj Sharma Alias Girraj Kumar ... vs State Of U.P. "A.

sentences.text:
That both the parties have mutually agreed that the First party will not pursue the FIR No. 0189/2021 U/S 420/406/323/504/506 of 1. P. C. registered at P.S.
Alambagh District Lucknow keeping in mind the paramount interest of each other previous good relations which was converted into business and at present ready to continue their business in future if the economical condition of parties allowed.
B.

That both parties are also agreed that second party will not pursue FIR No.
0312/2020 U/S 420/ 406/504/ 506 of I. P. C. registered at P.S. Alambagh District Lucknow.
Both parties during the session of Mediation process and also sitting outside of mediation process meet out their grievances which was arising out of Letter of intent dated 30.01.2018.

C. That both parties to solve their financial dispute have decided that the first party Giriraj Shrma @Giriraj Kumar Sharma (First Party/Petitioner) will provide a cheque bearing no 161714 dated 15.12.2022 of State Bank of India Branch Jiwajiganj Mandi,
Morena of Rs.25,00,000/- (Rupees twenty five lakh) only to the second party Rakesh Kumar (Second Party/Opposite Party No. 2) at the time of agreement as full and final settled amount and this cheque will be a part of agreement.
D. That it has been agreed mutually between the parties that they will not go for any litigation against each other in future.
E. That it has been agreed mutually that both will respect the dignity of each other in the paramount interest of pious business relationship and will maintain the same with utmost sincerity.

F. That it is also agreed between the parties that neither they themselves nor any member of their respective families shall institute any case in the form of criminal or civil proceedings against each other, or any of their relative or family members, in future in respect to the present dispute or any matter incidental thereto and if any proceeding has already been initiated the same would be get disposed of in terms of this settlement Agreement.
G.
That both the parties shall be bound by the terms and conditions of this Settlement in strict sense.
In case of any default, the party committing default shall be liable for playing fraud with the Court, hence for contempt of the Court."

7. Accordingly, the applicant Giriraj Shrma @Giriraj Kumar Sharma was to provide a cheque bearing no.161714 dated 15.12.2022 of State Bank of India, Branch Jiwajiganj Mandi, Morena of Rs.25,00,000/- to Rakesh Kumar at the time of agreement as full and final settled amount and the cheque was to be a part of the agreement.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the aforesaid cheque bearing no.161714 dated 15.12.2022 issued from State Bank of India, Branch Jiwajiganj Mandi, Morena of Rs.25,00,000/- was given to Rakesh Kumar at the time of signing the agreement before the Mediation Centre.
The aforesaid cheque as given to the opposite party bounced on 21.12.2022.

9. Learned counsel for the applicant being aware of the condition as detailed in the agreement before the Mediation Centre immediately sent the amount of Rs.25,00,000/- through RTGS in the account of Rakesh Kumar on 23.12.2022.
The aforesaid fact is evident from Page-6 of the short rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant on 20.09.2023.

10. Learned counsel for the opposite party, however, submits that as per the agreement before the Mediation Centre Rs.25,00,000/- was only a part payment and for the rest of the amount the matter was yet to be settled.
He further submits that the amount as deposited through RTGS by the applicant on 23.12.2022 is some other amount which was given by the opposite party to the applicant.

11. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
12.

The Court at this stage cannot entertain the submissions as made by learned counsel for the opposite party as the settlement agreement dated 15.12.2022 has been placed on record, according to which, in paragraph 6-C as mentioned above, the terms and conditions have been mentioned,
wherein the amount was towards full and final settlement and the cheque was given at the time of signing the agreement.

The money so deposited through RTGS was as a precaution taken by the applicant to fulfill the terms and conditions of the agreement in order to comply with the agreement,
so that no fault may come before this Court on his part.

It is highly improbable to believe that a person who is having a dispute of Rs.2/- Crores with any person, which was initiated in the year 2020 by means of lodging an FIR, would give any other amount for some other transaction, for which the amount of Rs.25,00,000/- has been deposited through RTGS as alleged by learned counsel for the applicant.

13. In view of the above as well as terms and conditions as mentioned in the agreement dated 15.12.2022, which have been complied in totality, the charge sheet dated 25.02.2021,
cognizance/summoning order dated 22.07.2021 as well as bailable warrant dated 20.04.2022 issued by learned Judicial Magistrate-3, Lucknow, arising out of FIR No.312/2020 dated 25.11.2020 lodged at Police Station-Alambagh, District- Lucknow, under Sections 420, 406, 504, 506 I.P.C., are quashed.
14. The Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. stands allowed.
